scene: SKIP: reporting is speech; the scene reads as vertellen or praten (review M9).

one adult stands beside a plain table with one arm stretched out and only the tip of the index finger meeting the side of a standing glass; the glass is upright and steady and still stands clear of the table edge, the arm not yet bent.
must: a straight index finger just touching the side of an upright glass.
avoid: a flat palm resting on a table edge (leggen); an open hand closing on a glass to lift it (pakken); a fist striking a nail (slaan); the glass tipped over on its side; a spark or a flash at the fingertip.
alt: Iemand tikt met de top van de wijsvinger tegen de zijkant van een rechtopstaand glas.
example_nl: De bal raakt de muur.
example_en: The ball hits the wall.

scene: one adult stands facing a second adult and holds up an unfolded sheet of paper at chest height with both hands, turned so the sheet faces the other person; that person leans in with both eyes on the sheet. The sheet is a plain white oblong with no letters on it.
must: an unfolded blank sheet held up at chest height, turned to face a second person.
avoid: a box passing from hand to hand between two people (geven); two people with a bar each above the head (praten); one adult leaning close to a framed picture on a wall (bekijken); a person pointing with a straight finger (wijzen); text on the sheet.
alt: Iemand houdt met twee handen een vel papier omhoog naar een ander, die voorover kijkt.
example_nl: Kunt u uw paspoort tonen?
example_en: Can you show your passport?

scene: one adult sits at a plain table bent over a sheet with one large outline drawn on it, a crayon pressed to the paper and half the outline already filled with close hatching; a second crayon lies beside the sheet.
must: an outline half filled with hatching and one crayon pressed to the paper.
avoid: a pencil scribbling a line that copies nothing (tekenen); four crayons lined up in a row (kiezen); an easel with a brush and wet paint (schilderen); a bucket of paint with a brush dipped in it; a colour chart.
alt: Iemand vult op papier een grote omtrek half met dichte arcering; een tweede krijtje ligt ernaast.
example_nl: De kinderen kleuren een plaatje.
example_en: The children colour a picture.

scene: one adult runs onto an empty bus stop with one arm stretched out after a bus that has just pulled away, the bus already two lengths off at the right edge with its doors shut; the runner's mouth is open and the shoulders drop.
must: an arm stretched after a bus that has already left the stop.
avoid: a person stepping up into an open bus door (instappen); a person standing calmly at the stop (wachten); a person running with nothing ahead (rennen); a hand waving goodbye at a window (zwaaien).
alt: Iemand rent een lege bushalte op en steekt een arm uit naar een bus die net wegrijdt.
example_nl: Ik ren, want ik wil de bus niet missen.
example_en: I am running because I do not want to miss the bus.

scene: SKIP: needing and not needing are modal meanings with no object in the world to draw; any picture of them would be a convention from the A0 and A1 brief, and those are not allowed on this page.
SKIP: organising is abstract, and the scene needed numbered cards, which is text in the artwork (review H5, M9).
SKIP: wishing is a private idea with no action; the birthday cake convention is idiom, and a clasped hands or candle picture would be the same wish token that hopen uses on the A1 page.

one adult stands beside a low trestle, seen from the side, full figure; a single solid thick bar (the plank) rests flat on top of the trestle; the saw blade runs horizontally from the adult's near hand into a narrow V-shaped notch cut into the plank's top edge, with the blade's toothed lower edge inside the notch, halfway through; the saw never crosses the plank's front face; the free hand rests flat on the plank; a little sawdust lies under the cut. A second plank leans against the trestle.
must: a toothed saw halfway through the top edge of a clamped plank.
avoid: one adult at a table nailing planks into a crate (maken); a screwdriver turning in a broken chair leg (herstellen); a knife cutting bread on a board (snijden); a tree lying felled on the ground; a machine saw with a guard.
alt: Iemand beweegt een getand blad door een plank op een schraag; fijn houtstof valt onder de snede op de grond.
example_nl: Mijn vader gaat het hout zagen.
example_en: My father is going to saw the wood.

scene: one adult is caught mid-step with both heels lifted and the toes on the floor, the hips swung to one side, one arm curved up above the head and the other out to the side, chin up and eyes closed. Both feet stay near the floor and nothing else is in the picture.
must: one adult with both heels lifted, hips swung and one arm curved above the head.
avoid: both feet off the ground with the body stretched up (springen); two people facing each other holding hands and turning in a circle (draaien); a person walking in a straight line past a chair (lopen); music notes in the air; a stage and a crowd.
alt: Een volwassene staat op de tenen met de heup opzij en een arm gebogen boven het hoofd.
example_nl: Wij dansen op het feest.
example_en: We dance at the party.

scene: SKIP: serving as something or being of use is a relational meaning with no action of its own; a waiter carrying a tray would be the single picture of brengen or geven on other pages.

one adult stands facing a wall-mounted tap with both hands already closed on the round handle, the wrist just twisted and one drop of water falling from the spout. The body is turned slightly towards the wall, elbows lifted, eyes on the spout. The single water drop is the same solid cobalt as everything else, with no lighter tint; the hand holds the handle directly on the tap, with no pipe or line hanging down from it.
must: a round tap handle caught mid-turn with one drop leaving the spout.
avoid: a person turning on the spot to face the other way (keren); two people turning in a circle hand in hand (dansen); a door pushed nearly shut (sluiten); a key standing in a lock; a hand on a steering wheel.
alt: Twee handen houden een ronde kraanhendel vast; er valt een druppel uit de tuit.
example_nl: De wielen van de fiets draaien snel.
example_en: The wheels of the bike turn fast.

scene: SKIP: developing is a slow change over time and has no single moment; any picture would need two frames or a before and after, and a person holding up a small seedling is the picture of planten on this page.
SKIP: a synonym of zetten and leggen; the tree scene was planten (review M8).

one adult sits on a low bench in a shoe shop and pulls a new shoe onto one foot, one finger at the heel; the other shoe stands beside its open box on the floor and a small mirror stands at ankle height. No price tag and no shop assistant. The shoe is a laceless slip-on: one hand holds it at the heel tab with a finger inside the heel, the other hand rests on the knee; no laces, loops or knots anywhere.
must: a shoe being pulled onto a foot beside its open box.
avoid: a lace tied in a bow (strikken); coins handed over a counter (betalen); a pair of shoes carried in a bag (kopen); a person walking in the shoes (lopen).
alt: Iemand zit op een bankje in een schoenenwinkel en trekt een nieuwe schoen aan, naast de open doos.
example_nl: Deze broek past me niet.
example_en: These trousers do not fit me.

scene: one adult in overalls stands at the open back of a small van holding a closed cardboard box out with both hands towards a second adult on a path; the box is halfway between them and the van's doors are swung wide. A hand truck leans at the van. Above the head of the adult in overalls delivering floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: a box held out from a van's open back to a person on a path.
avoid: a box passing between two people at a table (geven); one adult rolling a trolley along a shelf (boodschappen); a stack of boxes carried against the chest (dragen); a clipboard with a signature; a shop counter with a price.
alt: Iemand in een overall reikt bij een busje een doos aan naar een ander op het pad.
example_nl: Het bedrijf levert groente aan restaurants.
example_en: The company supplies vegetables to restaurants.

scene: SKIP: differing means comparing two things and reporting a difference, so the picture would be two objects plus an added comparison mark or number; the two-jars picture already belongs to kiezen on the A1 page.

one adult bends over a rubbish bin, one hand already holding a crumpled sheet of paper inside it and letting go, the fingers just opening; the bin is white and empty beneath. No other person and nothing else in the picture.
must: fingers just opening above a bin with the crumpled paper inside it.
avoid: a sheet held up before a second person (tonen); a page taken from a shelf into a bag (pakken); a broom sweeping a floor; a bin bag tied at the top; a hand held flat against the chest (houden).
alt: Iemand buigt boven een prullenbak en laat een verfrommeld vel papier in de bak vallen.
example_nl: Ik verwijder de oude foto's van mijn telefoon.
example_en: I remove the old photos from my phone.

scene: SKIP: determining is a judgement about what will happen and has no action in the world; a person marking one line on a chart would need a choice between objects, which is the picture of kiezen.

one adult sits at a plain table looking up at a second adult standing beside it; the seated adult has one hand lifted with the index finger raised and the mouth open in a single word, and no object lies between them. Above the head of the seated adult who is answering floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: one adult with a raised index finger looking up at another who stands and waits.
avoid: two people with a bar each above the head and one holding a sheet (spreken); a hand cupped behind an ear in a bare room (luisteren); an envelope pushed into a postbox slot (sturen); a telephone held to the ear; letters in the air.
alt: Iemand kijkt op naar een staande bezoeker en houdt een opgestoken wijsvinger bij een open mond.
example_nl: Hij antwoordt niet op mijn vraag.
example_en: He does not answer my question.

scene: SKIP: meaning is a link between a word and a thing and can only be drawn as a sign with an arrow or as lettering, both of which the brief forbids, and the sign would pair with tonen on this page.

SKIP: bordering is a line between two areas and needs two named countries; without letters it would be an unexplained fence line, and every fence on these pages already stands for a garden or a field.
SKIP: remembering is a private act that can only be drawn with the thought bubble convention, which belongs to denken on the A0 page and is not allowed here.

one child stands with their back to a wall, full figure, head turned slightly towards the wall; the wall has no outline, border, frame or panel at all, it is just white space. Draw only ONE vertical column of four marks on the wall: the child's flat raised palm pressed on the wall at the very top of the head is the topmost mark and nothing is drawn above it; the new short horizontal stroke is the first mark directly below the palm, with the adult's pencil tip touching it; exactly three more short strokes of the same length lower down, at waist height. Four marks in total, none above the hand. An adult kneels beside the child without overlapping the child's legs. Nothing to the right of the hand except the pencil.
must: a child's flat hand on a wall while an adult draws the line under it.
avoid: a small tree pressed into a garden hole (planten); seeds scattered over bare soil (zaaien); a scissors and a lock of hair (knippen); a tape measure held out; a row of numbered marks.
alt: Een kind staat tegen de muur; een volwassene zet een streep onder de hand op het hoofd.
example_nl: De planten groeien snel in de zomer.
example_en: The plants grow quickly in summer.

scene: SKIP: lasting is how long something takes and has no action; a person waiting under a clock is the picture of wachten on the A1 page, and a clock alone is an object, not a verb.

one adult holds a printed list in one hand and a pencil in the other, bending over three stacked crates on a hand truck, the pencil ticking the bottom line with the eyes on that line. A tin can stands open in the top crate.
must: a pencil ticking a list line above three stacked crates on a truck.
avoid: one adult leaning close to a framed picture on a wall (bekijken); a person with an eye to a microscope (onderzoeken); a finger held up beside a standing person (antwoorden); a crossed-out page in a bin (verwijderen); letters on the list.
alt: Iemand buigt over drie kratten en zet met een potlood een streep op een lijst.
example_nl: De conducteur komt de kaartjes controleren.
example_en: The conductor comes to check the tickets.

scene: one adult stands with the weight on the back foot, the front foot just lifting and the whole body turned sideways, one arm still stretched out high after the release and both eyes on a round ball already in the air a metre from the raised hand.
must: a ball in the air above a raised hand after the release.
avoid: the ball still in both hands and only the arms lifting it (werpen); both hands cupped low and the ball just leaving the fingers (spelen); a ball in the air and a raised racket (slaan); a ball in a goal net; an arrow or a dotted arc.
alt: Een bal hangt in de lucht naast een hoog uitgestoken arm; de voet voor is net los.
example_nl: De jongen gooit de bal naar zijn vader.
example_en: The boy throws the ball to his father.

scene: an aeroplane in side view comes down over a runway, its wheels a finger's width above the surface and the nose slightly up, with no smoke at the tyres; one plain stripe runs along the runway and the sky shows only one flat cloud.
must: an aeroplane with its wheels a finger's width above the runway.
avoid: a pilot at the controls high between clouds (vliegen); a closed cabin door with a grip on the handle (openen); a flat suitcase dropping through the air (vallen); a person walking down the cabin stairs (lopen).
alt: Een vliegtuig daalt boven een startbaan; de wielen hangen net boven het asfalt.
example_nl: Het vliegtuig landt om tien uur.
example_en: The plane lands at ten o'clock.

scene: two adults stand facing each other and hold hands, both smiling, and a thin ring sits on one of the joined fingers; the person on the left wears a plain white dress and the other a dark suit. Plain ground, no other person, no building.
must: two adults holding hands with a ring on one joined finger.
avoid: two people facing each other with a sheet between their hands (tonen); a family sitting at a set table (vieren); two people at a counter with a pen and a notebook (melden); a church spire or a town hall; two boxes with a bow (cadeau).
alt: Twee volwassenen staan hand in hand met een ring aan een vinger.
example_nl: Mijn zus gaat volgend jaar trouwen.
example_en: My sister is going to get married next year.

scene: one adult rides a bicycle from left to right along a plain road line, body upright and both hands on the handlebars; the right pedal is at the bottom of its circle with that leg straight and the other knee lifted, wheels on the ground, bag on a rear rack.
must: an adult upright on a bicycle with both feet on the pedals.
avoid: a person with no bicycle walking past a parked one (lopen); a car with brake lights close to a raised palm (stoppen); a bicycle standing still against a wall (zetten); a motorcycle with an engine; a helmet shown alone.
alt: Een volwassene rijdt rechtop op een rijwiel, de handen aan het stuur en een tas achterop.
example_nl: Ik fiets elke dag naar mijn werk.
example_en: I cycle to work every day.

scene: one adult stands at a stove with one hand holding the long handle of a pan while the other hand shakes a wooden spoon over it; steam rises in two bold curves, a pot lid lies to the side and a raw carrot stands on the counter.
must: nearly done food in a pan being stirred with a wooden spoon.
avoid: a tray of round buns going into a closed oven (bakken); a person holding a piece of bread to an open mouth (eten); a kettle pouring into a cup (drinken); a waiter with a tray (dienen); a cookbook propped open.
alt: Iemand roert in een pan op het fornuis terwijl er stoom boven opstijgt; de steel in de andere hand.
example_nl: Mijn vader kookt vanavond macaroni.
example_en: My father is cooking macaroni tonight.

scene: two adults meet on plain ground with their right hands already in a firm shake and the eyes on each other; the one on the right leans in and has one hand lifted towards the other's shoulder. No object lies between them and they stand a step apart.
must: two adults shaking hands and looking each other in the eye.
avoid: an open hand raised in a greeting at a doorway (kennen); one adult walking behind another (volgen); a sheet of paper held up between two people (tonen); arms around each other; a table with two chairs.
alt: Twee volwassenen geven elkaar een stevige hand en kijken elkaar aan.
example_nl: Wij ontmoeten onze buren in de tuin.
example_en: We meet our neighbours in the garden.

scene: one adult faces a closed door and pushes it with one flat hand on the panel while the other hand turns the handle; the gap at the edge is widening and a slice of the brighter room beyond shows through it. The person looks into that gap.
must: a widening gap of light at a door edge under one pushing palm.
avoid: a door pushed from inside until nearly shut (sluiten); an envelope torn at one end (opendoen); a hand pressing a light switch; a key turned twice in a lock; a key held up in triumph (vinden).
alt: Een hand duwt een deur van zich af; door de brede kier valt licht naar binnen.
example_nl: Zij opent de deur voor de gasten.
example_en: She opens the door for the guests.

scene: one adult kneels in a garden bed and presses a small plant with its root ball into a hole in the soil with both hands, the roots half in and half out of the dark earth. A hand trowel lies on the soil and a second plant waits in its pot.
must: a small plant's roots halfway into a fresh hole in the soil.
avoid: a seedling already standing upright with the arms lifted beside it (groeien); small seeds scattered over bare soil (zaaien); a spade pushed into a mound of earth (begraven); a pot standing on a windowsill; flowers in every colour.
alt: Twee handen leggen een stekje met de wortels in een vers gat in de tuinaarde.
example_nl: Wij planten bloemen in de tuin.
example_en: We plant flowers in the garden.

scene: One adult is crouched in a sprint start on two blocks at the beginning of an empty running track, fingertips on the line, the head down, the hips raised, one knee bent forward. The track runs straight ahead into the distance. No other runners, no crowd, no text.
must: a crouched runner with hands on the line and hips raised.
avoid: a runner at full speed with both feet off the ground (rennen); a person turning a key in a car (opstarten); a person walking on the track (lopen); a finish tape being broken (winnen); a person pressing a button on a computer (opstarten).
alt: Een volwassene zit gehurkt op twee blokken aan het begin van een lege baan, vingertoppen op de lijn, hoofd omlaag.
example_nl: De hardlopers starten over een minuut.
example_en: The runners start in one minute.

scene: one adult sits at a plain table with a pencil in one hand pressed to a sheet of paper, drawing one bold round shape; beside the pencil lie an eraser and a ruler, and a second sheet shows the same shape already drawn in outline.
must: one pencil point down on a sheet with a rounded shape partly drawn.
avoid: one adult filling in printed shapes with crayons (kleuren); a brush on an upright white canvas with paint pots (schilderen); a person with an eye to a microscope (onderzoeken); a finger held up beside an open mouth (antwoorden); printed letters on the paper.
alt: Iemand trekt met een potlood een ronde vorm op papier, met een gum en liniaal ernaast.
example_nl: Mijn dochter tekent graag paarden.
example_en: My daughter likes drawing horses.

scene: SKIP: creating is a general word for making something new and would take the picture of maken or bouwen; any distinct scene would be a second verb on this page for the same act, and no honest single action is left.

one adult stands on a riverbank bent forward with both hands on a long fishing rod, the line running down into the water and a float visible on the surface; a small bucket stands behind on the grass. The water is a plain band, not a sea.
must: a taut rod bent forward over water with a float on the surface.
avoid: an adult with arms out swimming in open water (zwemmen); a boat with a net lifted (varen); a fish already hanging on the line; a fish in a bucket; a person in a rowing boat.
alt: Iemand staat voorover aan de waterkant met beide handen aan een hengel en een dobber op het water.
example_nl: Mijn opa gaat zaterdag vissen.
example_en: My grandfather is going fishing on Saturday.

scene: one adult stands in a polling booth and slips a folded paper into a slot on the top of a plain box that has a small closed lid; the fingers are still on the paper, and a folded card lies on the shelf beside the box. No letters are on the paper or the card.
must: a folded paper slipping into the slot of a closed box.
avoid: a note pushed across a shop counter (betalen); a raised hand with fingers apart (spreken); a hand in a raised fist (kunnen); a ballot box already full with the paper gone.
alt: Iemand schuift een dichtgevouwen papiertje in de gleuf van een houten kistje.
example_nl: Vandaag mogen wij stemmen voor een nieuwe gemeenteraad.
example_en: Today we may vote for a new municipal council.

scene: one adult sits at a restaurant table with an open menu in both hands, one finger resting on a line, looking up at a second adult standing beside the table with a small notebook and a pencil ready. Plates and a jug are on the table. Above the head of the seated adult ordering floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: an open menu held up while someone with a notebook writes.
avoid: a folded newspaper held up in a chair (lezen); an envelope pushed into a slot (sturen); a tray carried between two tables (dienen); a plate of food already on the table (eten); a till with coins (betalen).
alt: Iemand wijst in een open menu aan en kijkt op naar iemand met schrift en potlood.
example_nl: Wij bestellen twee koffie en een broodje.
example_en: We order two coffees and a bread roll.

scene: one adult in a white coat stands at a workbench and holds a bicycle lamp pointed straight at a light meter, the needle of the meter already near the top of its scale; the meter is a blank dial with tick marks only and no text, letters or numbers on it; a bright plain cone shows between lamp and meter, drawn as a white-filled cone with a cobalt outline, the same cobalt as everything else; two loose wires lie on the bench.
must: a lamp pointed at a meter whose needle has swung up.
avoid: a pencil ticking lines on a list over stacked crates (controleren); a person with an eye to a microscope (onderzoeken); a sheet held up to a second person (tonen); a clipboard with letters; a battery in a tester.
alt: Iemand in een witte jas richt een fietslamp op een meter; de naald staat hoog.
example_nl: Wij testen het nieuwe programma vandaag.
example_en: We are testing the new programme today.

scene: one adult stands on the ground at the open back of a small lorry and lifts a closed cardboard box down off the empty lorry bed with both hands, the box clear of the bed and in the air, not set down; a neat stack of boxes already stands on the ground behind the adult, away from the lorry, and the lorry bed itself is empty; a hand truck leans against the bumper. Use exactly the same single flat cobalt as every other card, with no darker navy and no ground shadow ellipses or shading; both hands visibly grip the box's two sides, with the box in the air above the bed. Both hands are clearly visible, one on the left side and one on the right side of the box; the box is held directly over the empty lorry bed with the arms stretched toward the bed; keep every element at least 10% from the edges, with the stack of boxes smaller and moved in; one single flat ink tone only. The man's two hands grip the left and right sides of one box held in front of his chest; the box is in the air, outside the lorry, level with the empty bed; the lorry's cargo area is drawn as an empty outline with no boxes inside; the stack of boxes stands behind him.
must: a box lifted clear of a lorry, clear of the ground, above a row of boxes.
avoid: a box held out towards a second person at the van's back (leveren); one adult alone with a box pressed to the chest (houden); a man pushing a broom across a floor (vegen); a fork-lift truck; a stack of boxes with a tick list.
alt: Iemand tilt bij de open vrachtwagen een doos omhoog; op de grond staan al andere dozen.
example_nl: De chauffeur lost de dozen bij de winkel.
example_en: The driver unloads the boxes at the shop.

scene: SKIP: arranging is the same office action as organiseren on this page; a second picture of it at this level would duplicate that scene, which the brief forbids.

one adult runs at full stretch from left to right, both feet off the ground, arms high, the head turned back over one shoulder, a small bag clutched in one hand; far behind at the left edge stand a second adult with both fists raised.
must: one adult running away with both feet off the ground, head turned back.
avoid: an adult walking an ordinary stride past a chair (lopen); a person holding a bag against the chest with both hands (houden); a fistfight between two people (aanvallen); a lorry door being opened (lossen); a burning house or smoke.
alt: Iemand rent hard weg met losse voeten en kijkt over de schouder terug.
example_nl: De mensen vluchten voor het water.
example_en: The people are fleeing from the water.

scene: SKIP: treating is a sequence of care; the bandage is verbinden and the stethoscope is onderzoeken (review M8).

one adult kneels on the floor beside an open box and holds up a small flat card, three of those cards already lying in the box; one hand sorts the rest of a fanned pile, eyes on a card, and the box holds nothing else.
must: a card held up above a box that already holds three more.
avoid: one adult kneeling to reach under a sofa cushion (zoeken); coins pushed across a counter (betalen); a glass held down onto a table by one hand (zetten); a net and a butterfly; a full album with a row of photos.
alt: Iemand houdt een kaartje boven een open doos waarin er al drie liggen.
example_nl: Mijn broertje verzamelt oude munten.
example_en: My little brother collects old coins.

scene: SKIP: containing is a state, not an action; an open box with things in it is a picture of hebben or of verzamelen, and an arrow into the box would be a symbol the brief does not allow here.

one adult at a plain desk speaks into a telephone held to one ear while one finger presses a date on an open paper calendar: a square on the calendar is circled in dark ink. No laptop, no second person, and the calendar shows no digits.
must: a telephone at one ear beside a calendar with one circled day.
avoid: a phone at the ear with no calendar and no second person (bellen); both hands on a suitcase handle at a desk edge (pakken); a note pushed across a counter (betalen); a passport in a raised hand.
alt: Iemand heeft een telefoon aan het oor en wijst een omcirkelde dag op een kalender aan.
example_nl: Wij boeken een hotel aan zee.
example_en: We book a hotel by the sea.

scene: one adult is caught sinking to their knees on plain ground: one knee already down, the other leg folding under, both hands open and out to break the fall, the hips low and the mouth open. The body is still above the ground and nothing else is in the picture.
must: a person halfway down to the floor with both hands out.
avoid: an adult tipping forward with both arms flung out and no hand down (vallen); a hammer raised high over a nail (slaan); a person sitting on a low stool with the back straight (zitten); a person on the floor pushing up with one hand (opstaan); a flat arrow pointing down.
alt: Iemand gaat met één knie naar de grond, de andere vouwt eronder en beide handen zijn open.
example_nl: De temperatuur zakt vannacht onder nul.
example_en: The temperature drops below zero tonight.

scene: SKIP: belonging is ownership or membership, which is a fixed relation and not an action; a name tag on a coat or a house key would need letters or would read as hebben.
SKIP: struggling with something is a state of trouble, not a pictureable action; the closest literal scene would be two people wrestling, which the brief would read as aanvallen on this same page.
SKIP: surviving is only visible after a disaster and needs a context of ruin to make sense; a person alone with a torn coat at a wrecked building would read as a destitute stranger, not as this verb.

one adult sits in a chair with one bandaged leg stretched out on a low footstool and a crutch propped beside the chair, reaching down with one hand to lift a cup from a small side table. A folded newspaper lies on the knee, and nothing else is in the room.
must: a bandaged leg up on a stool and a hand reaching for a cup.
avoid: one adult at a workbench turning a screwdriver in a broken chair (repareren); a person bent over a table nailing planks (maken); a knee and both hands hitting the ground (zakken); a hospital bed; a medicine bottle.
alt: Iemand zit met een verband om het been op een voetenbankje, een kruk ernaast, en pakt een kop.
example_nl: Mijn vader herstelt snel na de operatie.
example_en: My father recovers quickly after the operation.

scene: SKIP: the key found in the soil is the drawing of vinden (review M8).

one adult sits alone at a library table with a thick open book in front of them, elbows on the table and the head propped on one hand, a pen moving on a page of notes; three more closed books are stacked beside it and a lamp stands on the table.
must: one adult alone at a table with an open book and a pen writing notes.
avoid: two people bent over one book with a finger on the page (leren); one adult at a laptop at a desk (werken); a framed picture looked at on a wall (bekijken); a classroom with a blackboard; letters on the page.
alt: Iemand zit alleen aan een tafel met een dik open boek, hoofd op een hand en pen in de andere.
example_nl: Zij studeert geneeskunde in Leiden.
example_en: She studies medicine in Leiden.

scene: SKIP: witnessing is the second person in a scene, so the picture would be an onlooker with no distinguishing mark; it would duplicate ontmoeten or aanvallen depending on what is watched, and a raised right hand would be a courtroom idiom.

one adult stands with one shoulder under the arm of a second adult who leans heavily with a bandaged ankle, one arm around the first's neck; the helper's other hand is flat on the leaning person's back, and both walk. The leaning person's near arm is draped across the back of the helper's neck and shoulders with the hand hanging over the far shoulder; the helper's near hand is flat on the leaning person's back and the helper's shoulder is under the leaning person's armpit. The leaning man's near arm lies across the back of the helper's neck and shoulders with the hand hanging over the far shoulder; the helper's near hand is flat on the leaner's back at waist height, seen from behind or beside; the helper's arm stays off the leaner's shoulders. The leaning man's arm lies across the back of the helper's neck and shoulders; nothing of the helper's arm goes over the leaner's shoulders or round his waist; the helper's hand is flat on the leaner's back with the fingers visible against the leaner's torso.
must: a leaning person's arm over another's shoulder, one hand flat on the back.
avoid: one person lifting a box with both hands (lossen); two people with their hands clasped and a gold ring (trouwen); a hand laid on a table edge (raken); a walking stick alone; coins dropping into a hat (betalen).
alt: Iemand laat een manke ander op de schouder leunen, de arm om de nek en een hand op de rug.
example_nl: Wij steunen onze vriend na het ongeluk.
example_en: We support our friend after the accident.

scene: one adult sits at a plain table with a big blank weekly planner lying open; one hand slides a small block with a finger across the page and a group of empty squares below is marked in dark ink. A pen stands upright in a holder, and no letters or digits appear. The grid squares are empty outlines, with a few solid filled squares as the marked ones and no crosses or letters; the planner and table are smaller, with at least 10% white margin on every side.
must: a finger sliding one block across a grid of marked empty squares.
avoid: a phone at the ear over a calendar with one day circled (boeken); a hand turning the cover of a closed notebook (beginnen); a person walking away leaving keys on a table (vergeten); a note pushed across a counter (betalen).
alt: Iemand schuift met een vinger een blokje langs de vakjes van een open weekschema.
example_nl: Wij plannen een reis naar Italië.
example_en: We are planning a trip to Italy.

scene: SKIP: accepting is inner; a handshake or a hand taking something reads as afspreken or pakken.

one adult sits on a bench with tears running down both cheeks, the mouth turned down and the eyebrows raised in the middle, one hand holding a crumpled tissue near the face. Nobody else is in the picture.
must: tears running down the cheeks of a downturned face.
avoid: tears with a wide open laughing mouth (lachen); a wide yawn with the eyes shut (gapen); knuckles rubbing tired eyes (moe zijn); raindrops on the face under a cloud (regenen).
alt: Iemand zit op een bank; tranen lopen over beide wangen en een hand houdt een zakdoek vast.
example_nl: Het kind huilt om zijn speelgoed.
example_en: The child cries over his toy.

scene: SKIP: practising is repetition of some other activity, so the single picture would be whichever activity is drawn (spelen, schrijven, sporten).

one adult sits at a plain desk with a wooden frame abacus in front of them, one finger pushing a single bead along its rod while the other hand holds a pencil over a blank pad; eyes on the beads. No digits on the pad, no screen, nothing else in the picture.
must: a finger pushing a bead along the rod of an abacus.
avoid: a finger touching apples in a row one by one (tellen); a calculator with a display of numbers; a pen writing a long line on paper (schrijven); a coin purse and notes (betalen); any digit or sign.
alt: Iemand zit aan een bureau en schuift met een vinger een kraal langs de stang van een telraam.
example_nl: Ik kan goed rekenen.
example_en: I am good at arithmetic.

scene: two adults walk slowly side by side on a plain path; the one on the right is older and leans a little, and the one on the left holds that person's elbow with one hand and the back with the other, looking at them. Nothing else in the picture.
must: one adult holding another's elbow and back as that person leans on them.
avoid: two people carrying one box between them (helpen); a hug with both arms round the neck (omarmen); a person pushing a wheelchair; a person lifting a heavy shelf; a hand patting a shoulder.
alt: Iemand houdt een oudere persoon bij de elleboog en de rug vast terwijl die leunend loopt.
example_nl: De gemeente wil de familie ondersteunen.
example_en: The municipality wants to support the family.

scene: one adult sits on a plain bench in profile with one hand raised to the mouth holding a lit cigarette between two fingers; a thin curl of smoke rises from the tip, and the other hand rests on the knee. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a cigarette between two fingers at the mouth with a thin curl of smoke.
avoid: a cup raised to the mouth with steam (drinken); a pipe-shaped bubble toy; a fire or flames; a crossed-out cigarette sign; a person coughing into a fist.
alt: Iemand zit op een bank en houdt een brandend sigaretje bij de mond; een dun wolkje stijgt op.
example_nl: Mijn oom rookt buiten op het balkon.
example_en: My uncle smokes outside on the balcony.

scene: SKIP: a complaint is speech with a grumpy tone; the picture would be a person talking (praten) or frowning at a broken object, which is boos or kapot.

no person: one single row of bold shoe-shaped footprints leads straight up the page towards a closed gate and then bends sharply round in a tight U-turn and comes back down alongside itself; the footprints are thick and clear; the gate is a plain bold outline at the top. Nothing else.
must: footprints that go forward and then turn back on themselves.
avoid: a person turning a round tap handle with both hands (draaien); a person walking away towards the horizon (lopen); two people turning in a circle (dansen); a person looking over a shoulder at a left-behind key (vergeten); a curved arrow.
alt: Voetafdrukken lopen naar een hek en draaien daar weer om.
example_nl: We moeten keren, we zijn te ver gereden.
example_en: We have to turn back, we have driven too far.

scene: SKIP: noticing is a mental event; a person looking at a small thing would read as zien or kijken, and the thought bubble is only allowed for A0 and A1.
SKIP: characterizing is an abstract relation between a trait and a thing; no action exists to draw.
SKIP: realizing is a flash of understanding; the only picture is the lightbulb bubble, which belongs to weten and is not allowed at A2.
SKIP: defending has three unrelated pictures (arguing, guarding a goal, shielding someone), so no single drawing is honest; they would read as praten, vangen or beschermen.

one bird flies up and out through a wide open cage door, the cage drawn as a plain bold-outlined cage with a few bars and the door swung open; the bird is already outside the door in the air with its wings spread. No person.
must: a bird flying out through an open cage door.
avoid: a person climbing over a wall with a ladder (klimmen); a person running with nothing behind (rennen); an open cage door with a bird; a person unlocking a door with a key (openen); a person lying on a sofa with arms spread (ontspannen).
alt: Een vogel vliegt door de open deur van een kooi naar buiten.
example_nl: De gevangene probeert te ontsnappen.
example_en: The prisoner tries to escape.

scene: one picture divided into four equal panels in a two-by-two grid by thick cobalt lines, each panel holding one simple sport pictogram with a whole figure from head to feet: top left a tennis player swinging a racket at a ball, top right a footballer kicking a ball, bottom left a swimmer crawling in water drawn as a wavy line, bottom right a hockey player with a stick hitting a puck; nothing else, no text.
must: four small panels showing four different sports.
avoid: a person running with both feet off the ground (rennen); a coach with a stopwatch beside a ball and cones (trainen); a person asleep on a mat (slapen); a person digging (graven); a barbell.
alt: Vier vakjes met een tennisser, een voetballer, een zwemmer en een hockeyspeler.
example_nl: Ik sport twee keer per week.
example_en: I exercise twice a week.

scene: one adult strolls at an easy pace along a winding path over a gentle hill, hands behind the back, a small backpack and a hat, one walking stick planted in the ground at the front; a single tree and a bench stand beside the path. Seen from the side, caught mid-step.
must: a relaxed stroller with a walking stick on a winding country path.
avoid: a brisk stride on empty ground with swinging arms (lopen); both feet off the ground (rennen); a bicycle beside the person (fietsen); a rope and a steep cliff (klimmen); a dog on a lead.
alt: Iemand slentert met een stok en een rugzakje over een kronkelend pad langs een boom en een bank.
example_nl: Wij wandelen zondag door het bos.
example_en: We are going for a walk in the woods on Sunday.

scene: SKIP: investing is financial and abstract; a plant growing out of coins is a metaphor that exists only in idiom, and bags of money would read as betalen or sparen.

two adults stand close and face each other in profile; one leans in with closed eyes and presses the lips lightly to the other's cheek, while the other stays still with a slight smile. Nothing else in the picture, no heart symbols.
must: one adult pressing the lips to another's cheek.
avoid: a hug with both arms round the shoulders (omarmen); a handshake (groeten); two faces near each other with a speech bubble (praten); hearts or flowers; two adults who are pressing noses.
alt: Twee mensen staan dicht tegenover elkaar; de een drukt met gesloten ogen de lippen tegen de wang van de ander.
example_nl: Zij komt mij op de wang kussen.
example_en: She comes to kiss me on the cheek.

scene: one adult stands at the open back of a small van carrying one cardboard box in both arms towards a house front door; more stacked boxes and a floor lamp stand beside the van, and the house door is open. The adult looks at the door.
must: a person carrying a box from a loaded van towards a house door.
avoid: a box passing from hand to hand between two people (geven); a person walking with a suitcase to a train (reizen); a person assembling a box (maken); a for-sale board; a crowd of movers.
alt: Iemand draagt een kartonnen doos uit een bestelwagen vol dozen naar de open voordeur van een huis.
example_nl: Wij gaan volgende maand verhuizen.
example_en: We are moving house next month.

scene: two adults on a plain pavement: the one on the left lifts an arm in a wave and leans forward towards the other; the one on the right walks straight past with eyes fixed ahead, face blank, not turning the head. No other objects.
must: one person waving and the other walking past without turning the head.
avoid: two people shaking hands (groeten); two people waving at each other (zwaaien); one person with arms folded and a frown (boos); one person with eyes on a phone; one person running away.
alt: Iemand zwaait naar een ander die recht vooruit kijkt en zonder het hoofd te draaien langsloopt.
example_nl: Hij probeert zijn buurman te negeren.
example_en: He tries to ignore his neighbour.

scene: SKIP: causing is a relation between events; any drawing (a spilled glass, a collision) would show a different verb and a before and after.

one adult stands beside a desktop printer on a small table, one hand resting on its lid, watching a single blank white sheet that is half out of the front slot; a small stack of blank paper sits beside it. No screen, no text on the sheets.
must: a blank sheet coming half out of a desktop printer.
avoid: a finger pressing a doorbell button (duwen); a hand pressing down on a stamp pad (stempelen); a person writing by hand with a pen (schrijven); a book on a shelf; a crate being pushed.
alt: Iemand staat naast een bureauprinter waaruit een leeg vel papier half naar buiten komt.
example_nl: Deze boeken zijn in Nederland gedrukt.
example_en: These books were printed in the Netherlands.

scene: no person: a plain plank ramp slopes down to the left, and one single plain solid ball sits on the ramp surface about halfway down; nothing else in the picture, no floor marks, no motion lines.
must: a ball on a sloping plank.
avoid: a ball thrown through the air (gooien); a person kicking a ball (voetballen); a person pressing dough flat with a rolling pin (bakken); a wheel on a bicycle (fietsen); speed lines or dust puffs.
alt: Een bal ligt halverwege op een schuine plank.
example_nl: De bal rolt van de tafel.
example_en: The ball rolls off the table.

scene: one adult sits at a plain table with a straight row of five apples in front of them; the index finger of one hand touches the third apple, the other hand rests flat beside the row, and the eyes follow the finger. No digits, no pad.
must: a fingertip touching the third apple in a row of five.
avoid: a bead pushed along an abacus rod (rekenen); a hand taking an apple from the row (pakken); a person writing on paper (schrijven); a pile of coins (betalen); a basket full of apples.
alt: Iemand zit aan een tafel en wijst met een vinger de derde appel aan in een rij van vijf.
example_nl: Het kind kan al tot twintig tellen.
example_en: The child can already count to twenty.

scene: two adults on an open sports field: a player dribbles a ball in a slalom between a row of cones, and a coach stands to the side holding a stopwatch in one hand with the other arm pointing along the row. Both look at the cones.
must: a coach with a stopwatch beside a player dribbling a ball between cones.
avoid: a person doing a push-up on a mat (sporten); a match with two teams (spelen); a person running alone (rennen); a classroom with a board (leren); a person lifting a barbell.
alt: Een volwassene stuit een bal tussen pionnen door terwijl een ander met een stopwatch in de hand toekijkt.
example_nl: Onze club traint op woensdagavond.
example_en: Our club trains on Wednesday evening.

scene: SKIP: demanding is a tone of voice; the picture would be a person talking (praten) or an open hand held out (vragen) with an angry face (boos).
SKIP: explaining is speech; any drawing reads as vertellen or praten, and a pointer at a board is lesgeven.

one adult courier in a plain jacket stands at a house front door, sets a medium cardboard parcel down on the doormat with one hand and presses the doorbell button with the other; a cargo bike with a box stands at the kerb. The door is closed and nobody else is in the picture. The parcel rests on the doormat with the courier's hand just lifted off it; the door is a flat outline in the same single cobalt with no lighter side panel or stripe. The parcel rests flat on the doormat with both of the courier's hands empty of it and one hand pressing the bell; the door is a plain outline with no inner frame, panel or light stripe. The courier stands upright beside the door; one hand is raised and its finger presses the round bell button; the other arm hangs empty at the side; the parcel sits alone on a plain doormat drawn as a bare rectangle with no hatching; the door is a bare rectangle outline with no inner frame line. Every line is thick and bold; any bicycle is a simple bold-outline shape with solid wheel discs and no spokes; the parcel sits fully inside the doormat rectangle, clear of the step, with no tape line.
must: a parcel set down on a doormat in front of a closed door.
avoid: a box passing from hand to hand between two people (geven); a person carrying a box into a new house (verhuizen); a person posting a letter into a box (sturen); a person at a shop counter with a bag (kopen); a ribbon on the parcel.
alt: Iemand zet een pakket op de deurmat voor een gesloten deur; een bakfiets staat bij de stoeprand.
example_nl: De postbode bezorgt de pakketjes om twee uur.
example_en: The postman delivers the parcels at two o'clock.

scene: one adult stands at a plain table and pours water from a glass jug held in one hand into a tall glass standing on the table; the water in the glass has reached just below the rim and a thin stream still runs from the jug. The adult watches the water level.
must: a stream from a jug into a glass with the water just below the rim.
avoid: an empty glass tipped over on its side (leegmaken); a kettle pouring into a cup with steam (koken); a hand lifting a full glass to the mouth (drinken); a jug and a glass standing apart; drops flying over the table.
alt: Iemand giet vanuit een glazen kan water in een hoog glas; het water staat bijna tot de rand.
example_nl: Ik vul de fles met water.
example_en: I fill the bottle with water.

scene: one adult runs from left to right over empty ground, caught with both feet off the ground, the body leaning forward, the arms bent and pumping in opposition, mouth slightly open and eyes ahead. Nothing else is in the picture.
must: both feet off the ground with the body leaning forward at speed.
avoid: one foot flat on the ground and the other just lifting, the back upright (lopen); a person upright on a bicycle (fietsen); a straight raised knee and a stiff swinging arm (marcheren); a stopwatch; speed lines or dust puffs.
alt: Een volwassene is met beide voeten van de grond en leunt voorover met gebogen, zwaaiende armen.
example_nl: De jongen rent snel naar de bushalte.
example_en: The boy runs quickly to the bus stop.

scene: SKIP: thanking is a spoken act whose usual gestures (a bow, a palm on the chest, a gift) read as zijn or cadeau, and a speech bubble is not allowed.
SKIP: convincing is a change of mind with no action; any picture would be two people talking, which reads as praten.
SKIP: adding is putting one more item on a pile; the only picture is a hand placing a block, which is the leggen card.
SKIP: succeeding is an outcome, not an action; a raised fist or a trophy would be a convention outside A0 and A1.

one adult stands with feet apart and both hands cupped around the mouth, the head thrown back and the mouth wide open, looking across empty ground at a small distant figure at the right edge of the frame. No speech bubble, no letters.
must: two cupped hands at a wide-open mouth aimed at a far-off figure.
avoid: two adults facing each other close by with a bar each above the head (praten); a mouth open in a song with a microphone (zingen); a face with tears on the cheeks (huilen); a hand cupped behind an ear (luisteren); speech bubbles or lettering.
alt: Een volwassene houdt beide handen als trechter voor een wijd open mond en kijkt naar een verre figuur.
example_nl: De supporters schreeuwen luid in het stadion.
example_en: The supporters shout loudly in the stadium.

scene: SKIP: raising a quantity has no object to draw; a stack of blocks would read as stapelen and an arrow is a symbol.
SKIP: the only picture is a person replying to another, which is exactly the antwoorden scene already drawn on another page.
SKIP: downloading is an arrow or a progress bar on a screen, which is a symbol and needs text or numbers; a laptop alone would read as werken.
SKIP: strengthening is abstract; the flexed arm is the convention for kunnen and is not allowed here.
SKIP: spending is paying for something, so the picture would be coins on a counter, which is betalen.

one adult stands a metre back from a campfire of three crossed logs on bare ground, the arms at the sides and the face lit; bold flames rise from the logs and one log has gone dark at the ends. No smoke cloud, no tent, no other person.
must: bold flames rising from crossed logs with a person standing back.
avoid: a pot on a stove with a spoon (koken); a hand pulled back from a hot pan (pijn doen); a candle on a table; a house with flames at the windows; a bucket of water thrown on the logs.
alt: Een volwassene staat op afstand van een kampvuur; hoge vlammen slaan uit drie gekruiste houtblokken.
example_nl: De open haard brandt de hele avond.
example_en: The fireplace burns all evening.

scene: SKIP: daring is a private state of nerve; a person at a cliff edge would read as springen and any other symbol is not allowed.
SKIP: acting has no action of its own and trading would read as kopen or verkopen.
SKIP: borrowing and lending are one hands-over scene that cannot be told apart from geven or nemen without a text or a note.
SKIP: spelling means saying letters aloud, which needs lettering in the drawing, and the word also means playing a game.
SKIP: stimulating is an abstract pushing of a process; any picture would be a person encouraging another, which reads as praten or helpen.
SKIP: enlarging is a before and after change in size; a magnifying glass would read as zoeken and two frames are not allowed.
SKIP: destroying is the same picture as breaking or demolishing, and a person smashing something would be violent and shared with verwijderen.
SKIP: informing is passing on facts, so the picture would be a person talking or showing a sheet, which reads as praten or tonen.
SKIP: confirming is a nod with no object, and the picture would be the knikken picture.
SKIP: keeping is not doing anything to an object; a jar on a shelf would read as zetten and a person hugging a box as houden.
SKIP: producing is making many things in a factory, which would be a crowd of objects or the maken scene.
SKIP: recognising is a private act that can only be drawn with a thought bubble or a pointing hand, which belong to denken and wijzen.
SKIP: spreading news or a rumour is abstract, and spreading butter or seed would read as smeren or strooien instead.
SKIP: succeeding is a result with no action of its own; a trophy or raised arms would read as winnen.
SKIP: limiting is abstract; a fence or a cut-off line would read as afsluiten or a rule rather than the verb.
SKIP: the only picture is a coin dropped into a piggy bank, which is sparen, and the sense of sparing someone a trouble cannot be drawn.
SKIP: communicating is two people with a bar each above the head, which is praten on the A1 page.

one adult stands in a plain room holding a wooden chair off the floor with both hands, carrying it from the left side towards a pale square marked on the floor at the right, one step taken. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a chair lifted off the floor and carried from one spot to another.
avoid: a person dragging a chair along the floor (slepen); a person sitting down on the chair (zitten); a box carried to a doorway (dragen); a trolley pushed along (duwen); arrows or dotted paths.
alt: Iemand draagt een stoel met twee handen van de ene plek in de kamer naar een andere plek.
example_nl: Wij verplaatsen de kast naar de andere kamer.
example_en: We move the cupboard to the other room.

scene: two adults stand facing each other an arm's length apart. The one on the left holds out a plate with a slice of cake; the one on the right holds one flat open palm up and forward to keep it away, chin turned slightly aside, eyes on the plate. Above the head of the person refusing (palm up) floats one bold solid cobalt arrow pointing straight down at the head, with a clear white gap between arrow tip and hair; it marks who performs the verb. The other person has no arrow. No text.
must: a flat palm held up against an offered plate while the head turns away.
avoid: a plate handed over and taken in both hands (geven); a person eating the cake (eten); a hand raised in a wave (zwaaien); only a head shaking with no plate (nee zeggen); a crossed-out symbol.
alt: Twee mensen staan tegenover elkaar; de een biedt een bord met taart aan, de ander houdt een open hand ervoor.
example_nl: De hond weigert te eten.
example_en: The dog refuses to eat.

scene: SKIP: thanking is a spoken act; a nod or bow would read as groeten or buigen, and a handed-over box would read as geven.
SKIP: committing a crime or an act is abstract, and any picture would be the crime itself, such as stelen, rather than plegen.

two adults stand facing each other an arm's length apart, each holding out one object to the other: the left person an apple, the right person a loaf of bread. Both objects are caught halfway, side by side between the two pairs of hands. Both look at what they are about to receive.
must: two different objects passing in opposite directions between two people.
avoid: one box passing one way only (geven); coins and notes on a counter (betalen); two people shaking hands (groeten); a shop shelf with a price (kopen); a ring of arrows.
alt: Twee mensen staan tegenover elkaar en houden elk een ander voorwerp naar de ander uit; de voorwerpen kruisen elkaar.
example_nl: Wij wisselen vandaag onze telefoonnummers.
example_en: We exchange phone numbers today.

scene: SKIP: a decision has no single picturable action, the same as besluiten; a fork in the road would read as kiezen and a gavel as rechtspreken.

one adult sits leaning back on a plain park bench, arms spread along the backrest and legs stretched out and crossed at the ankle, eyes open and looking at the sky, shoulders loose. Nothing else in the picture.
must: a person leaning fully back on a bench with loose shoulders and stretched legs.
avoid: a person lying in bed with closed eyes (slapen); a person sitting upright at a table (zitten); a person on a cushion with a book (lezen); a cup or a phone in the hand; zzz marks.
alt: Iemand zit achterover op een bankje met de armen langs de rugleuning en de benen uitgestrekt.
example_nl: Na het werk wil ik even rusten.
example_en: After work I want to rest for a bit.

scene: SKIP: striving is an inner aim with no single action; an arrow at a target or a climber would read as richten or klimmen.

one adult stands on the left leg in an empty yard, the right leg swung forward at the moment of impact, the foot just meeting a tin can that is lifting off the ground at the right. The adult looks at the can. No goal and no ball. There are no motion arcs near the can and no marks on the ground; the ground is one plain straight line, or none.
must: a swung foot meeting a can that is leaving the ground.
avoid: a ball shot into a goal (scoren); a leg lifted for a step, with the can untouched (lopen); a foot on a bicycle pedal (fietsen); a fist striking the can (slaan); speed lines or dust puffs.
alt: Iemand staat op een been en schopt met de andere voet tegen een blikje dat van de grond komt.
example_nl: Hij trapt een leeg blikje van de stoep.
example_en: He kicks an empty can off the pavement.

scene: SKIP: reducing is a quantity going down; a shrinking pile or a falling arrow would need extra symbols and has no action of its own.

one adult follows through after a shot on a small grass pitch, standing on the left leg with the right leg still swinging up; a football sits in the back of a goal net at the right, the net bulging behind it, and the goalkeeper is not drawn. Draw the goal as an open frame with several net lines (bold outline only, no fill), the ball resting at the back against the net, and a short grass baseline.
must: a football lying in the net of a goal, with the kicker still in follow-through.
avoid: a foot hitting a tin can in a yard (trappen); a person dribbling a ball down the pitch (voetballen); a player with raised arms and a trophy (winnen); a ball flying wide of the goal; a scoreboard.
alt: Iemand zwaait na een schot het been door; de bal ligt achter in het net van een doel.
example_nl: Onze spits scoort in de laatste minuut.
example_en: Our striker scores in the last minute.

scene: SKIP: processing has no single action: it means working material, digesting news or coping, and each picture would read as a different verb.
SKIP: getting used to something is a gradual inner change with no single moment to draw.
SKIP: promoting is abstract; a person lifted a step up a ladder would read as klimmen or a job promotion rather than the verb.
one adult stands side-on, full figure head to feet, holding a boxy video camera up to one eye with both hands, the lens pointing straight ahead; nothing else in the picture.
must: an adult with a video camera held to one eye.
avoid: a phone held up for a still picture (fotograferen); a person watching a television (kijken); a spotlight and a clapper board; a flash; a tripod with nobody behind it.
alt: Iemand houdt met beide handen een videocamera voor het oog.
example_nl: Mijn zus filmt de kinderen in de tuin.
example_en: My sister films the children in the garden.

scene: SKIP: a greeting is a wave or a handshake, which are zwaaien and the handshake on other pages, and a nod has no single clear mark.
SKIP: hatred is an emotion with no action; a scowling face is boos and clenched fists are woede, and nothing separates it at thumbnail size.

one adult stands facing a closed plain door and knocks on it with the knuckles of a bent hand held at head height, the other arm hanging at the side; the door has a handle and no window, no sign, and no bell. Only the person and the door are in the picture.
must: knuckles meeting a closed door.
avoid: a hand pressing a doorbell (bellen); a hand turning the handle (openen); a fist hitting a person (slaan); a mallet on a nail (hameren); sound marks.
alt: Iemand staat voor een dichte deur en tikt met de knokkels van een gebogen hand tegen het hout.
example_nl: Iemand klopt zachtjes op de deur.
example_en: Someone knocks softly on the door.

scene: One adult stands at a kitchen counter, holding a small bowl steady with the left hand and cracking an egg against the rim with the right; the shell is split and the yolk is dropping into the bowl. Two whole eggs lie on the counter. Nothing else in the picture.
must: an egg split at the rim of a bowl, the yolk dropping in.
avoid: knuckles on a closed door (kloppen); a fork stirring eggs in a bowl (mengen); a hand turning a knife through a carrot (snijden); a hand pressing a doorbell (bellen); a pan of eggs already set on the hob (bakken).
alt: Een volwassene breekt een ei boven een kom en laat de dooier in de kom vallen.
example_nl: Ik klop twee eieren in een kom.
example_en: I beat two eggs in a bowl.

scene: One adult stands on a station platform with one arm raised high and the open hand waving, fingers spread, face smiling, looking at a train that is pulling away to the right with a small face at its window. Platform only, no other people.
must: a raised open hand waving at a departing train.
avoid: a person swinging a flag over the head (zwaaien); two people shaking hands (schudden); a hand held up flat to halt a car (stoppen); a person calling with a hand beside the mouth (roepen); a person running after the train (missen).
alt: Een volwassene staat op een perron met een hoog opgestoken open hand en kijkt naar een trein die wegrijdt.
example_nl: Ze zwaait naar haar opa bij het raam.
example_en: She waves at her grandpa at the window.

scene: Two adults stand facing each other an arm's length apart, smiling, their right hands clasped together at the middle between them in a handshake. Both look at each other's face. Plain background, no objects, no text.
must: two right hands clasped between two smiling people.
avoid: a bottle shaken up and down in one hand (schudden); a hand waving in the air (zwaaien); two people hugging (omhelzen); a box passed between hands (geven); a person bowing (buigen).
alt: Twee mensen staan tegenover elkaar en pakken elkaars rechterhand vast; ze lachen en kijken elkaar aan.
example_nl: Hij schudt de nieuwe collega de hand.
example_en: He shakes the new colleague's hand.
